purpose: Region cards and page headers: still renders and short turntable loops of simLAB's own joint models.
license: CC BY-SA 4.0. The models derive from the AnatomyTool Open 3D Anatomical Model (Leiden University Medical Center and collaborators) with Z-Anatomy and BodyParts3D lineage. These renders are adaptations and carry the same license.
method: three.js 0.183 GLTFLoader in headless Chromium. Bones only (capsules, ligaments, muscles, cartilage and discs hidden), one bone colour, room-environment lighting with a green rim light, ACES tone mapping, a 360° turn about the vertical axis. Frames are composited onto the card gradient; video is VP9 WebM with an H.264 MP4 fallback at 30 fps. The whole-body skeleton is mirrored about the midline because the source model is one side. No image editing or generation beyond framing and compositing.

hero.note: Home hero tiles. Each is a 4:3 loop at 480x360, 24 fps, VP9 WebM with an H.264 MP4 fallback and a first-frame WebP poster. No image editing or generation beyond framing, compositing and the burned-in labels.

tiles.method: three.js 0.183 render of the knee bones turning once, with the native artery and vein, nerve, and muscle and tendon layers swept in from below, deep to superficial, then peeled back in reverse by a world-space clipping plane. Composited on the card gradient.

tiles.source: simLAB movement lab, PROM · Hip flexion (exam-prom-hip-flexion), right side, male model, run locally from danstonedev/simlab with its pinned submodules
tiles.method: Frame-by-frame captures of the lab's own stage (supine patient, examiner hands, goniometer) stepped along its movement timeline at 24 fps, cropped to 4:3. The renderer-name check was overridden only so the headless software renderer drew at full resolution.

tiles.source: simLAB eye and vestibular lab, Horizontal canal BPPV (geotropic): supine roll (eye-bppv-horizontal-geotropic), left, run locally
tiles.method: Captures of the lab's stage, close on the patient as the head turns from midline to the left (39.7 to 42.5 s of the exam), then its Frenzel close-up (43 to 47 s) with both ears' canal views from the same moments, all real time at 24 fps. Recomposed into 4:3 with labels.

tiles.source: simPACS (danstonedev/simpacs at 199a4d0, pose-engine a38450b), lower-limb model, run locally
tiles.method: Screen captures of the simPACS reconstruction viewport on the full-body model: an AP X-ray projection cropped to the left shoulder, then coronal CT (soft-tissue window) and MRI T1 slices through the left shoulder stepped across 60 mm, cropped and cross-faded. Labels name the modality and plane.

hero.license: Anatomy CC BY-SA 4.0 (AnatomyTool Open 3D Anatomical Model, LUMC et al., via Z-Anatomy and BodyParts3D).

headers.note: Region and topic page header tiles. Each is a loop of the resource the tile links to, at 480x360, 24 fps, VP9 WebM with an H.264 MP4 fallback and a first-frame WebP poster. The Imaging topic reuses hero-imaging. Single-resource topics open their resource directly and have no header. No image editing or generation beyond framing, keying and compositing.
headers.license: Anatomy CC BY-SA 4.0 (AnatomyTool Open 3D Anatomical Model, LUMC et al., via Z-Anatomy and BodyParts3D).
